name: fab
title: FAB
description: The one primary action of a screen, floating over its content at the bottom inline-end corner.

base.summary: A primary button in shape and colour, held to a corner of the viewport. The fill and its label token are Button's primary pair unchanged, because this is the screen's primary action and nothing about floating changes that.

tokens.color: theme.fg.on-accent — the one label token that belongs on theme.accent-role.bg
tokens.inline-size, label hidden: equal to the block-size, so the hidden-label FAB is a circle
tokens.border-radius: radius.pill — one radius that makes the hidden-label FAB a circle and the labelled one a pill, so the two are visibly the same control
tokens.hover / press: compose the .rata-state-layer class — do not swap the background
tokens.focus ring: theme.focus-ring at focus.ring-width, offset focus.ring-offset, on :focus-visible — never offset 0, because this is a filled accent control

placement.summary: Where it floats. Measured from the viewport's safe area rather than its edge, and lifted clear of a BottomNav when one is on the page.

tokens.placement center: inset-inline-start 50% with a translate of half its own inline size, in place of inset-inline-end
tokens.clearance above a BottomNav: when `:root:has(.rata-bottom-nav)`, inset-block-end adds the bar's own block size — computed from the same tokens BottomNav's recipe uses, so nothing is measured at runtime
tokens.z-index: above page content and below the top layer — a Dialog, Sheet or Menu opened from it must cover it, and they do, because the top layer is above every z-index

behavior.summary: A `<button type="button">` fixed to a corner of the viewport, with Button's activation, loading and disabled behaviour. No primitive of its own: it composes `getButtonProps`, because activation is identical and a second implementation of it is a second place for the aria-disabled guard to go wrong.

decisions.decision: It is a component, not a Button with a className
decisions.why: This system's test for a new component is a difference in semantics, and a FAB has none: it is announced as a button and activated as one. What it adds is a placement that every consumer would otherwise hand-write — fixed to a corner, offset by the safe-area inset, lifted clear of a BottomNav — and that is exactly the kind of value that ends up as `bottom: 72px` in a stylesheet and wrong on the next phone. It composes Button's primitive rather than restating it, so the only new thing is the geometry.

decisions.decision: One per screen, and always the primary fill — so there is no `variant`
decisions.why: A FAB says 'this is what this screen is for'. Two of them say nothing, and a secondary-styled one is a primary action that has been told to look unimportant while still floating over everything. The fill is Button's primary pair because it is the primary action; a destructive action never floats, because the one control that is always under the thumb is the last one that should delete something.

decisions.decision: `label` is required and shown by default
decisions.why: A floating glyph is the least explained control on a screen: it is detached from any content that could give it context. So the label is visible unless `labelHidden` is set, the same default and the same prop name as Switch. When it is hidden it becomes the `aria-label`, and it is still required, because an icon-only button with no name is announced as 'button' — this is Button's `iconOnly` obligation, enforced by the type instead of the contract.

decisions.decision: It does not shrink or hide on scroll
decisions.why: Collapsing a labelled FAB to its icon on scroll, or sliding it off-screen, is common and has the problem BottomNav's contract names: it moves a target out from under a thumb that was about to use it. It also changes the accessible name's visibility mid-gesture. The vertical space it saves is one control's worth in one corner.

decisions.decision: Reading order follows the DOM, so where it is rendered matters more than where it floats
decisions.why: Fixed positioning moves the paint and not the tab order. Rendered after a long list, the FAB is reached by keyboard only after every row in it; rendered at the start of `<main>`, it is reached first, which matches its importance. The contract cannot choose this for the caller, so it says it: render it before the content it acts on.

decisions.decision: It covers content, and the page reserves space for that
decisions.why: A fixed control sits over whatever scrolls beneath it, so the last row of a list ends behind it. BottomNav avoids this by being sticky; a FAB cannot, because it floats in a corner rather than spanning an edge. The page's scrolling content needs `padding-block-end` of at least the FAB's block size plus its offset — the recipe states both in tokens, so the reservation is a sum of the same tokens rather than a measured number.

decisions.decision: A speed dial is a Menu, not a mode of this
decisions.why: A FAB that fans out into three smaller actions is a trigger and a transient list of actions, which is precisely Menu — focus moves into it, Escape returns to the trigger, the arrow keys move between items. `<Menu trigger={<Fab … />}>` gets all of that from a component that already owns it; a `speedDial` prop here would be a second, unreviewed menu.

decisions.decision: `loading` and `disabled` behave exactly as they do on Button
decisions.why: Both are aria-disabled: the FAB stays focusable and discoverable and activation is blocked in the primitive. `loading` shows a Spinner in place of the icon and keeps the label, so the FAB does not change size while an action is pending. They are mutually exclusive for Button's reason — a control cannot be both busy and unavailable.

The hit area is size.target.min, 48px, on every platform — Material's minimum, which also clears Apple's 44pt and WCAG 2.5.5. It sizes where the control can be tapped, never the drawn box. Settled by the token interview (docs/decisions/2026-11-gate-1-review.md).

A FAB is persistent and floats over moving content, which is neither raised (a resting card), overlay (a transient surface anchored to a trigger) nor modal. theme.elevation.floating is that role. It points at the same primitive as overlay today, and is a separate role so a theme can strengthen one without the other. A menu opened from the FAB still uses overlay. Settled by the token interview (docs/decisions/2026-11-gate-1-review.md).

On the web it renders `<button type="button">`, position fixed, with `aria-label={label}` only when `labelHidden` is set — otherwise the visible text is the name, and the icon is `aria-hidden`. While `loading` it carries `aria-disabled="true"` and `aria-busy="true"`. On React Native it renders a `Pressable` with `accessibilityRole="button"`, `accessibilityLabel={label}`, and `accessibilityState={{ disabled, busy: loading }}`, absolutely positioned inside the screen and offset by `useSafeAreaInsets()`. Web-only: `className`, and the BottomNav clearance, which is a CSS `:has()` rule — a native screen knows its tab bar's height from the navigator and offsets by that instead. No prop is native-only. There is no gesture. Rata-drawn (decision N5): iOS has no floating action button and Android's is a Material library component rather than an OS control, so it is a drawn `Pressable` from the same recipe on both. The native implementation ships in the pro tier (decision N6).

decisions.decision: BottomNav publishes the clearance; the FAB reads it
decisions.why: Decided at gate 3. The recipe's clearance rule is ':root:has(.rata-bottom-nav)' adding the bar's block size. Written in fab.css, that selector names BottomNav's class, so the FAB would depend on a component it works without and 'rata add fab' would install it. So bottom-nav.css sets '--rata-bottom-nav-block-size' on ':root:has(.rata-bottom-nav)', summed from the tokens it draws the bar with, and fab.css adds 'var(--rata-bottom-nav-block-size, space.0)' to its safe-area offset. Same condition, same sum, and the sum sits beside the bar it measures. The bar's size includes its own safe-area padding, so on a notched phone the FAB clears the bar by space.padding.md plus the inset. That is the recipe's sum taken literally. A BottomNav hidden with 'display: none' still matches ':has()', so the FAB keeps the clearance at widths where the bar is hidden.

label.summary: What the action does, as a verb phrase — shown beside the icon, or used as the accessible name when hidden.
dont: A noun alone ('Invoice'), which says what the screen is about rather than what the button does.
label.a11y: The accessible name in both states. Visible text when shown; `aria-label` when `labelHidden` is set.

icon.summary: The glyph, which is always shown.
use: A glyph that means the action on its own — a plus for create, a pencil for compose.
dont: A brand mark or an illustration. Above `size.icon.lg` a graphic is no longer an icon, and the FAB's size is fixed.

labelHidden.summary: Shows the icon alone, as a circle, with `label` as the accessible name.
use: An action so conventional on its screen that the glyph explains it — the plus on a list of notes.
dont: Saving space on a screen where the action is not obvious. The label is what explains a floating control, and a circle with a glyph in it saves one word's width.
labelHidden.a11y: The name does not change; only whether it is visible.

placement.summary: Which bottom corner it floats at — inline-end, or centred.
use: `center` when the screen's content is symmetrical and the action belongs to all of it, such as a camera's shutter.
dont: `center` above a BottomNav. It lands over the middle destination's label and reads as a sixth item.
placement.a11y: Visual only; reading order follows the DOM, not the corner.

loading.summary: Shows a Spinner in place of the icon and blocks activation, while staying focusable.
use: The action's request is in flight and a second press would send it twice.
dont: As a page-loading indicator. The FAB is busy only with its own action.
loading.a11y: `aria-disabled="true"` and `aria-busy="true"`, as on Button. The label stays, so the name does not change while it is pending.

disabled.summary: Blocks activation while keeping it focusable and announced.
use: The action exists on this screen but cannot run yet, and the reader should be able to find out it exists.
dont: Permanently. A FAB that can never be pressed on a screen should not be rendered there — a disabled control floating over everything is the most prominent thing on the screen, and it does nothing.
disabled.a11y: `aria-disabled`, not the `disabled` attribute, so it stays in the tab order and screen readers announce it as unavailable rather than skipping it.

className.summary: Extra classes, for placement adjustments — not for restyling it.
use: Hiding it at widths where the action lives in a toolbar instead.
dont: A hand-written `bottom` offset. The placement is computed from the safe area and the BottomNav; a fixed number is wrong on the next device.

usage.case: Creating the thing a list is a list of
usage.when: A screen that is mostly one collection, where adding to it is the reason the screen exists.
usage.notes: Rendered at the start of `<main>`, before the list, so a keyboard reaches it first. The list reserves `padding-block-end` so its last row is not left under the FAB.

usage.case: A conventional glyph with the label hidden
usage.when: The action is the one every reader of this screen expects, and the glyph is its well-known mark.
usage.notes: `label` is still required: it becomes the `aria-label`. Hiding it is the exception, not the default, because nothing near a floating control explains it.

usage.case: Several creation actions behind one FAB
usage.when: A screen where the primary action is 'add', and there are two or three kinds of thing to add.
usage.example:
<Menu label="Add" trigger={<Fab label="Add" icon={Plus} />}>
  <MenuItem onSelect={addPhoto}>Photo</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem onSelect={addNote}>Note</MenuItem>
</Menu>
usage.notes: This is the speed dial, and it is Menu's job: focus moves into the list, Escape returns to the FAB, arrow keys move between items.

usage.case: Reaching for the wrong component: two floating actions
usage.when: A screen with a primary action and a secondary one, both wanting to float.
usage.notes: Don't. Two FABs is no primary action. Discard is not something to keep under the thumb at all — it belongs in a footer or a Menu, as a Button or a destructive MenuItem.
